BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Update & Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary: reject the "pre-cleared / STANDARD" framing

Before the substance, the most important point. The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asserts that every `[STANDARD]` clause has been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and asks us to scrutinise only `[OPEN]` items — but *nothing* in this package is actually marked `[OPEN]`, and the effect is to wave through the entire limitation and disclosure package without review.

Per our playbook (sec 0.4 / 6.3), a position is not "agreed", "final", "standard" or "cleared" merely because the counterparty's document says so. None of these have been through our authority process. **We treat every clause as live and open.** I'd flag this framing explicitly in our response so there's no later suggestion we acquiesced by silence.

---

## Material departures from our playbook

**1. General liability cap — Cl 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)**
Our baseline is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / 4,800,000 figure *matches our conditional fallback* — but that fallback is usable **only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given.** The number coinciding with a fallback does not clear it (playbook sec 6.3). Push back to 25% / 6,000,000.

**2. Thresholds — Cl 12.2**
Seller proposes de minimis **AUD 25,000** (vs our 5,000), basket **AUD 250,000** (vs our 50,000), and *excess-only* recovery above the basket. Our position is a first-dollar (tipping) basket once exceeded, not deductible/excess-only. All three are materially worse than playbook. Reject.

**3. Time limits — Cl 12.3 / 13**
Seller wants **18 months**. Our baseline is **24 months**; 18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Also reject the sweep-up that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" — this is the mechanism that silently drags fundamental/title/tax/fraud into the general regime. Push for 24 months and carve-outs.

**4. Fundamental / Title collapsed into general regime**
Seller proposes capacity and title warranties take the **same cap and time limits** "for administrative simplicity." This directly violates our requirement for a **separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** Firmly reject — this is not administrative, it caps our title/capacity recovery at 20% for 18 months.

**5. Fraud / wilful concealment carve-out — absent**
Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" with **no fraud carve-out**. Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent — non-waivable. This is a hard requirement. Insert the carve-out.

**6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2**
Seller relies on **whole-data-room + public-register deemed disclosure** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed data room," plus public records). Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Require **specific fair disclosure** only. Note §1.4 also disclaims that anything is "legally required" — fine as a non-admission, but it does not convert general disclosure into fair disclosure.

**7. Buyer knowledge — Cl 8.3**
Blanket exclusion of any matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." Our playbook says **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.** Any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. The "discoverable" limb is especially objectionable (constructive/imputed knowledge). Reject.

**8. Bluefen consent — Cl 3 / 6.3 + Disclosure §2**
Seller offers **"reasonable endeavours" and consent treated as satisfied on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied** yet. Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — a material customer. Our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**, not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. Make this a hard condition precedent.

**9. Riverlark — Cl 2 / 7 + Disclosure §3**
Seller proposes a **post-Completion release**. Facility ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, not repaid, no discharge included. Our playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given). Push for repayment/discharge at Completion.

**10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) — funds flow + Disclosure §5**
AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses are **deliberately not itemised** in the funds flow ("a matter for the Seller"), and on-costs (payroll tax, super) are not addressed. Our playbook requires these to be a **specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them.** Insist on explicit treatment so the economics don't leak onto the buyer (note debt-free/cash-free). Confirm on-costs are captured.

**11. Ironquay IP — Cl 11.1 + Disclosure §4**
Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment and declared "adequate." Our playbook says **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but **not independently verified** either way, and there's no receipt/assignment in the data room. Risk is loss of IP/materials, broader than one payment. Broaden the indemnity; don't accept "adequate."

**12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — Cl 4.6 / Sch 6 + Disclosure §6**
Seller downplays as "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material." Consistent with our playbook: **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** (§6 confirms scope/access/notification unresolved; ~1,240 records). Don't accept a dismissive characterisation, but equally don't assert a breach. Require: **preserve logs, complete the investigation, and provide updates**, plus an appropriate indemnity/condition pending resolution.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) — Disclosure §8**
Seller labels these "ordinary-course operating costs." Three related renewals at 110,000 each; disclosure doesn't confirm whether unavoidable/terminable/accrued. Our playbook: **assess — no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** So we neither accept the seller's "ordinary course" label nor book it as debt. Diligence the terms.

**14. Title — Disclosure §10 (DD-012 register)**
Seller evidences 100% ownership **solely by the Company's own share register (DD-012).** Our playbook: DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.** Note §10 itself concedes the Buyer hasn't completed verification.

**15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"**
Seller treats tax and IP as settled within the general cap/time regime. Our playbook keeps **Tax/IP as OPEN** — no unlimited liability assumed, but **no resolution either.** Reject the "settled" characterisation and the hidden general-regime override; keep these categories separate.

**16. Office lease (§7) / Mossvale (§9)**
Seller's reading — notification only, no landlord/Mossvale consent triggered by a share sale — may well be correct, but we should verify the actual change-of-control / assignment wording ourselves rather than accept the characterisation. Lower priority than the above but worth confirming in diligence.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Push-back |
|---|---|---|
| Framing | "Pre-cleared/STANDARD" | Reject; treat all clauses as open, state so expressly |
| 1 | General cap | 25% / AUD 6m; 20%/4.8m needs Frost authority (none) |
| 2 | Thresholds | de minimis 5k, basket 50k, first-dollar not excess-only |
| 3 | Time limit | 24 months; strike "all Claims" sweep-up; 18m needs Frost |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside general bars |
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | Insert; carve out of all caps/baskets/limits/remedies/non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room/register deemed |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Delete blanket; limit to named persons + reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Bluefen | Effective consent + conditions satisfied as CP; not consent-on-delivery |
| 9 | Riverlark | Payout + direct repayment + discharge at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Itemise/seller-fund AUD 420k + on-costs; no silent exclusion |
| 11 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Preserve/investigate/update; no admission, no dismissal |
| 13 | Sandbar | Assess; no auto-debt, no price cut |
| 14 | Title | Independent evidence; DD-012 insufficient |
| 15 | Tax/IP | Keep OPEN and separate; reject "settled" |

**Authority flags for you:** Several seller positions (20% cap, 18-month period, post-Completion Riverlark release) sit exactly on our *fallback* numbers but **cannot be accepted without Amelia Frost's written, draft-specific authority, which has not been given.** The coincidence of numbers does not clear them.

**No concessions to confirm as agreed.** Everything above remains to be negotiated from our baseline. Want me to draft the mark-up / response letter next?
